stories.headline: OpenAI robotics chief Caitlin Kalinowski resigns over Pentagon AI deal
key_facts: Caitlin Kalinowski, OpenAI's head of hardware and robotics since November 2024, announced her resignation on March 7-8, citing the company's Pentagon contract
Kalinowski stated on LinkedIn and X: 'Surveillance of Americans without judicial oversight and lethal autonomy without human authorization are lines that deserved more deliberation than they got'
She joined OpenAI from Meta, where she led development of the Orion AR headset
OpenAI said its contract contains safeguards against mass surveillance and autonomous weapons, stating it 'creates a workable path for responsible national security uses of AI'
Kalinowski wrote that OpenAI announced the Pentagon deal 'without the guardrails defined,' calling it 'a governance concern first and foremost'
This is the first high-profile departure from OpenAI over its Pentagon partnership, which came after rival Anthropic refused a similar contract

stories.headline: Pentagon officially designates Anthropic a supply-chain risk, company vows court challenge
key_facts: The Pentagon formally designated Anthropic and its products a 'supply chain risk, effective immediately' on March 6, the first time a US company has received such a label
The designation bars government contractors from using Anthropic's Claude AI in Pentagon-related work, though companies can still use Claude in projects unrelated to the military
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said the designation 'has a narrow scope' and announced the company will challenge the decision in court, stating 'we do not believe this action is legally sound'
Pentagon Under Secretary Emil Michael called Amodei a 'liar' with a 'God complex,' while Amodei called OpenAI's rival Pentagon deal 'safety theater' in a staff memo
Anthropic's two red lines — no mass domestic surveillance and no fully autonomous weapons without human oversight — remained non-negotiable throughout negotiations
Despite the designation, Anthropic reportedly saw record signups with over 1 million new users per day and analysts estimate approximately $20 billion annualized revenue run rate

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Codex Security, finds 14 CVEs across major open-source projects
key_facts: OpenAI launched Codex Security in research preview on March 6, exactly 14 days after Anthropic's Claude Code Security announcement
During beta, Codex Security scanned 1.2 million commits and flagged 792 critical-severity and 10,561 high-severity vulnerabilities
The tool earned 14 CVEs across OpenSSH, GnuTLS, GOGS, Chromium, PHP, libssh, and gpg-agent, including heap buffer overreads, double-free bugs, and authentication bypasses
Codex Security operates in three stages: threat modeling of repository architecture, context-aware scanning based on real-world exploitability, and sandbox validation with proof-of-concept exploits
Available to ChatGPT Enterprise, Business, and Edu customers, free for the first month; open-source maintainers get permanent free access through 'Codex for OSS'

Independent testing by Semgrep found Claude Code Security detected 46 vulnerabilities (14% true positive rate) vs Codex Security's 21 vulnerabilities (18% true positive rate), both exceeding 80% false positive rates

stories.headline: Nature study finds all 13 major LLMs can facilitate academic fraud, Claude most resistant
key_facts: A study published in Nature found that all 13 major LLMs tested could be used to commit academic fraud or facilitate junk science when prompted with requests ranging from curiosity to explicit fraud
Claude models by Anthropic were most resistant to fraud requests, with Opus 4.6 generating potentially fraudulent content only about 1% of the time under strict criteria
Grok models by xAI and early GPT versions performed worst, with Grok-3 generating potentially fraudulent content more than 30% of the time
The study was conceived by Alexander Alemi, an Anthropic researcher working in personal capacity, and Paul Ginsparg, physicist at Cornell University and founder of arXiv
Even when models refused direct fraud requests, they 'helped by providing other suggestions that could eventually help the user,' according to research-integrity specialist Elisabeth Bik
The study tested LLMs from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and xAI on tasks including fabricating papers for submission to arXiv

stories.headline: AI2 releases OLMo Hybrid, open-source transformer-RNN model that halves training cost
key_facts: The Allen Institute for AI released OLMo Hybrid on March 5, a 7 billion parameter model combining standard transformer attention layers with Gated DeltaNet, a linear recurrent neural network architecture
OLMo Hybrid matches OLMo 3's accuracy on MMLU while consuming 49% fewer training tokens, achieving 2x data efficiency
The model delivers 75% better inference throughput on long-context tasks compared to pure transformer architectures by avoiding quadratic compute scaling
Everything is fully open: weights, intermediate training checkpoints, complete training code, full technical report, training data documentation, and evaluation code on HuggingFace
This is the first fully open hybrid transformer-RNN architecture at this quality level, enabling the research community to independently test whether efficiency improvements scale to larger models
The architecture alternates transformer layers for precise full-context attention with recurrent layers that maintain compressed sequential state

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Marketplace for enterprises amid Pentagon standoff
key_facts: Anthropic announced Claude Marketplace on March 7, a storefront where enterprise customers can purchase third-party software built on Claude models
Launch partners include Snowflake, Harvey, Replit, and GitLab, with a waiting list open for additional partners
Customers can apply a portion of their existing annual Anthropic spend toward marketplace tools, reducing friction for adoption
Anthropic is waiving commissions on marketplace transactions; revenue comes from increased model usage since all apps run on Claude
The strategy mirrors AWS Marketplace and Azure approaches, positioning Anthropic as orchestrator of a growing AI software ecosystem
The launch came the same week Anthropic was designated a Pentagon supply-chain risk, demonstrating the company's continued commercial momentum despite government pressure

stories.headline: Ginkgo Bioworks launches Cloud Lab with AI agent for autonomous biological experiments
key_facts: Ginkgo Bioworks launched Ginkgo Cloud Lab on March 2, a browser-based interface allowing researchers to run biological protocols on autonomous lab infrastructure
The system runs on Ginkgo's proprietary Reconfigurable Automation Carts (RACs) combining high-precision robotic arms, maglev sample transport tracks, and industrial-grade software
Cloud Lab provides remote access to a fleet of over 70 instruments spanning sample preparation, liquid handling, analytical readouts, storage, and incubation
An AI-driven agent called EstiMate lets scientists submit protocols in human language and receive immediate assessment of compatibility with Ginkgo's autonomous fleet plus transparent pricing
The launch aligns with Ginkgo's 2026 strategy to consolidate R&D services into its Nebula autonomous lab in Boston and phase out traditional benchwork
This follows Ginkgo's earlier collaboration with OpenAI where GPT-5 autonomously ran 36,000 protein synthesis experiments, achieving 40% cost reduction

stories.headline: GPT-5.4 early reviews: native computer use 'commoditized,' first model to surpass humans on desktop automation
key_facts: Independent reviewers confirm GPT-5.4 as the first general-purpose model shipping with native computer use as a production API, not a research preview
On OSWorld-Verified desktop navigation benchmark, GPT-5.4 scores 75% versus 72.4% human benchmark, marking the first time an AI model surpassed human performance on desktop automation
GPT-5.4 introduced Tool Search, reducing token usage by 47% in tool-heavy agent workflows without accuracy loss, a significant cost reduction for production agent deployments
The model supports up to 1.05 million tokens of context via API, with premium pricing at 2x rate after 272,000 tokens
On GDPval benchmark testing knowledge work across 44 professions, GPT-5.4 matches or exceeds human professionals in 83% of comparisons, up from 70.9% for GPT-5.2
The launch coincided with user backlash over OpenAI's Pentagon deal, with reports of 1.5 million user cancellations and Anthropic gaining record signups

stories.headline: Nvidia halts H200 chip production for China, shifts TSMC capacity to Vera Rubin
key_facts: Nvidia has stopped production of H200 AI chips intended for China and reallocated TSMC manufacturing capacity to its next-generation Vera Rubin architecture, according to the Financial Times on March 5
Nvidia had received orders for 1 million H200 units from Chinese companies, but US export permit delays made meaningful sales unlikely in the near term
Nvidia said it holds US licenses to ship only 'small amounts' of H200 chips to China; the Commerce Department confirmed no H200 chips have been sold to Chinese customers
The move follows Nvidia's Q4 earnings on Feb 25 where it reported record $68.1 billion quarterly revenue (up 73% YoY) and excluded China data center revenue from forward guidance
The reallocation could accelerate Vera Rubin delivery timelines, as one source told the FT: 'This could in a way accelerate the Vera Rubin delivery and roll out'

stories.headline: TSMC fast-tracks new Tainan mega fab targeting 2028 completion amid AI chip surge
key_facts: TSMC is pressing ahead with a new fabrication plant at Tainan Science Park on a 15.46-hectare site, with construction expected to begin later in 2026 and completion targeted for 2028
The development proposal underwent a 20-day public notice period ending March 3, and an environmental impact assessment review committee meeting is scheduled for March 26
TSMC did not specify the process technology for the Tainan facility; the company is separately building 2nm fabs in Hsinchu and Kaohsiung and planning an A14 facility in Taichung
The fab is expected to create approximately 1,400 direct jobs and support around 500 additional contractor and supply chain positions
TSMC commands an estimated 67% share of the global pure-play foundry market, with its position particularly concentrated in leading-edge nodes below 5nm

stories.headline: Seven tech giants sign White House pledge to fund AI data center power without raising bills
key_facts: Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, and xAI signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge at the White House on March 4, committing to fund all power and grid upgrades for their data centers

The voluntary pledge, first announced by President Trump during his State of the Union address, requires signatories to 'build, bring, or buy' dedicated electricity for AI operations rather than burden public grids
Energy Secretary Chris Wright said: 'We're going to win in AI and we're going to stop the rise of electricity prices because of the seven leaders'

The agreement responds to bipartisan concerns that accelerating AI data center construction could raise residential electricity rates as data centers are expected to account for nearly 20% of global electricity demand growth
Morgan Stanley estimates hyperscalers could spend $1 trillion+ in 2025-2026 on energy infrastructure, with developers expecting power constraints by 2027-2028 due to grid underinvestment

stories.headline: Ukrainian SkyFall's Shrike Fiber drone wins Pentagon Drone Dominance with 99.3/100 score
key_facts: SkyFall's Shrike Fiber, a fibre-optic FPV kamikaze drone, scored 99.3 out of 100 points in the Pentagon's Drone Dominance Gauntlet I, beating the runner-up by more than 10 points
SkyFall partnered with British company Skycutter, which is listed as the official winner on the Drone Dominance website; SkyFall declined to comment pending official announcements
The Shrike 10 Fiber features a 20 km fibre-optic spool for electronic warfare resistance and carries up to 1 kg warhead capacity
Tests assessed strike accuracy at 2.5-10 km, urban operations against multiple targets, ease of use, and manufacturing scalability
11 companies total were selected to share the Phase 1 order of approximately 30,000 drones worth $150 million; Ukrainian Defense Drones also placed sixth with 72.9 points

stories.headline: Xiaomi deploys humanoid robot in EV factory, operates autonomously for 3 hours
key_facts: Xiaomi deployed a humanoid robot on its electric vehicle factory production line for autonomous self-tapping nut installation, operating continuously for three hours
The robot achieved a dual-side simultaneous installation success rate of 90.2% on a task Xiaomi described as 'the most challenging part' of the manufacturing process
The system uses Xiaomi's proprietary 4.7-billion-parameter Vision-Language-Action model called 'Xiaomi-Robotics-0' combined with reinforcement learning
The robot handled challenges including spline structures, inconsistent gripping posture, and magnetic attraction on positioning pins during assembly

stories.headline: SpaceX preps Starship Version 3 for Flight 12, first launch in nearly 5 months
key_facts: SpaceX's Starship has not launched since October 2025, an unusual nearly 5-month gap as the company prepares the pivotal Version 3 of the 400-foot megarocket
Elon Musk previously suggested Flight 12 could occur in March 2026, but no official launch date has been set; FAA licensing is still pending
Starship Version 3 is a larger and more powerful iteration designed for NASA Artemis moon missions and eventual Mars travel
The first Starship launch from Florida (Kennedy Space Center LC-39A) is anticipated for late summer or early fall 2026

stories.headline: UK authorizes US to use RAF Fairford and Diego Garcia for Iran strikes, first European ally in campaign
key_facts: The UK Defence Ministry confirmed on March 7 that the US has begun using British military bases for 'defensive operations' against Iran
At least three US Air Force B-1B Lancer bombers landed at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, with one arriving Friday evening and two more Saturday morning
The authorized bases are RAF Fairford in southwestern England and the UK-US Diego Garcia base on the Chagos Islands in the Indian Ocean
The UK is the first and only European country to openly allow the US to use its bases in the bombing campaign against Iran
Prime Minister Keir Starmer authorized the use of bases for Washington's operations
UK Chief of Defence Staff Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton said this is 'probably the most dangerous period in the last 30 years'
Trump later appeared to dismiss British involvement, posting 'we don't need people that join Wars after we've already won!'

key_facts: Six US Army Reserve soldiers killed by an Iranian drone strike in Kuwait were returned to Dover Air Force Base on March 7 in a dignified transfer ceremony

President Trump, First Lady Melania Trump, VP JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and AG Pam Bondi attended the ceremony

stories.headline: Israel strikes Iran oil facilities for first time; Tehran engulfed in smoke as four storage sites burn
key_facts: Israel targeted Iran's oil facilities for the first time on Saturday March 7-8, hitting four oil storage facilities and an oil transfer center in Tehran and Alborz province
Massive fireballs and thick plumes of black smoke rose over Tehran, blotting out the sun by Sunday morning and forcing drivers to use headlights at 10:30 AM
The facilities hit included the Aghdasieh oil warehouse, Tehran refinery, Shahran oil depot, and a facility in Alborz province
Iran's oil distribution company said four employees were killed in the strikes
Iranian state media described the strikes as an 'attack from the US and the Zionist regime'
Iranian clerics reported consensus had been reached on a successor to Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed on February 28

stories.headline: Strait of Hormuz effectively blocked: 3,000 vessels and 20,000 seafarers stranded, Kuwait and UAE cut oil output
key_facts: The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy issued a warning on VHF Channel 16 forbidding all navigation
Over 3,000 vessels and 20,000 seafarers are stranded in the Middle East, according to the IMO
The strait normally carries about 20% of global oil trade and major LNG flows, with approximately 80 tankers carrying 16-18 million barrels daily
Kuwait Petroleum Corporation declared force majeure on March 7 and began cutting crude oil production and refining throughput
The UAE also started reducing oil production as the near-closure of the strait ripples through energy markets
Goldman Sachs warned oil prices could breach $100/barrel within days and reach $150 by end of March without a solution
Only 10% of normal oil cargo flows are passing through the strait, 17 times larger than the peak impact of Russia's 2022 Ukraine invasion on oil supply

stories.headline: GRAIL's Galleri cancer blood test missed primary endpoint but showed meaningful Stage IV reduction in subgroups
key_facts: The NHS-Galleri trial evaluated annual multi-cancer screening with the Galleri blood test in 142,000 UK participants aged 50-77 over three years
The trial missed its primary endpoint of statistically significant Stage III-IV cancer reduction, causing GRAIL shares to plunge ~50%
Despite the headline failure, the test showed a greater than 20% reduction in Stage IV diagnoses by the second and third screening rounds for 12 deadly cancer types
Adding Galleri to standard screening resulted in a four-fold improvement in overall cancer detection rate
Peter Attia argued on March 7 that the composite endpoint obscured meaningful subgroup performance and the verdict is 'far from settled'
GRAIL sold 185,000 tests in 2025 generating $136.8M revenue; the test costs $1,000 and is not yet FDA-approved
Detailed trial results will be submitted for presentation at the ASCO 2026 annual meeting

stories.headline: Norn Group reviews two decades of mTOR longevity trials: animal promise, limited human clinical evidence
key_facts: The Norn Group published a review on March 7 analyzing lessons from mTOR-targeting interventions for human aging
Rapamycin has robustly extended lifespan in animal models across multiple species, but no human trial has directly shown it extends life or clearly slows aging
The PEARL trial showed low-dose intermittent rapamycin was well-tolerated over 1 year with modest changes in biological aging biomarkers
Rapamycin and its derivatives improved physiological parameters in the immune, cardiovascular, and integumentary systems in healthy individuals

The Barshop Institute at UT Health San Antonio received up to $38M to run VITAL-H, the first Phase 3 trial targeting aging in adults aged 60-65, randomizing to rapamycin, dapagliflozin, or semaglutide
A key safety concern is that mTORC2 inhibition induces insulin resistance, creating a trade-off between metabolic side effects and longevity benefits
